questions.stem: A person accidentally touches a hot pan and pulls their hand away before they consciously feel pain. Which part of the nervous system coordinated this rapid response?

options.text: The brain (cerebrum), which made a conscious decision to move the hand
The spinal cord, which coordinated the reflex action without waiting for the brain
The endocrine system, which released hormones to move the hand
The peripheral nerves, which acted independently without any coordination

questions.explanation: This is a reflex action coordinated by the spinal cord. The nerve impulse travels from receptor to sensory neurone to relay neurone in the spinal cord, then directly to a motor neurone without going to the brain first. This makes the response much faster, protecting the body from harm.

questions.stem: The nervous system is divided into the central nervous system (CNS) and the peripheral nervous system (PNS). Which structures make up the CNS?

options.text: All the nerves throughout the body
The brain and spinal cord
The sense organs and muscles
The sensory and motor neurones only

questions.explanation: The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord. It acts as the coordination centre, processing information from receptors and sending instructions to effectors. The PNS consists of all the nerves connecting the CNS to the rest of the body.

questions.stem: A patient suffers a spinal cord injury at the level of their waist. They lose feeling and movement in their legs but their arms are unaffected. What does this tell us about how the nervous system is organised?

options.text: Nerves from the legs connect to a different brain than nerves from the arms
Sensory and motor nerves from the legs enter and leave the spinal cord below the injury, so signals cannot pass the damaged area
The legs have their own independent nervous system
The injury has damaged the brain's ability to control all muscles

questions.explanation: Nerve impulses from the legs travel through the spinal cord to reach the brain. If the spinal cord is damaged at waist level, impulses from below that point cannot pass the injury to reach the brain (no sensation) and instructions from the brain cannot reach the leg muscles (no movement). Arm nerves connect above the injury and are unaffected.

questions.stem: A student compares the nervous system and endocrine system. Which statement correctly identifies a key difference?

options.text: The nervous system uses hormones; the endocrine system uses electrical impulses
The nervous system produces fast, short-lived responses via electrical impulses; the endocrine system produces slower, longer-lasting responses via hormones
The nervous system only controls voluntary actions; the endocrine system controls involuntary actions
Both systems operate at identical speeds and produce identical responses

questions.explanation: The nervous system transmits electrical impulses along neurones, producing rapid but short-lived responses targeted at specific effectors. The endocrine system releases hormones into the blood, producing slower but longer-lasting and more widespread effects. Both systems work together to maintain homeostasis.

questions.stem: In the pathway receptor → sensory neurone → CNS → motor neurone → effector, a person sees a ball flying towards them and ducks. What is the effector in this response?

options.text: The eyes (receptors that detected the ball)
The brain (which processed the information)
The muscles that contracted to make the person duck
The sensory neurones that carried the impulse

questions.explanation: An effector is the part of the body that carries out the response. In this case, the muscles are the effectors — they contract to make the person duck. The eyes are the receptors, the brain is the coordination centre, and the neurones are the pathways for impulses.
